guide.kicker: A LITTLE SETUP. A LOT OF FLOW.
guide.title: A few steps to get in the flow.
guide.description:
A little setup the first time.
Then open Settings from the menu bar or system tray.
guide.macTitle: How do I install and authorize on macOS?
guide.macOne: Unzip the download, move screen-buoy.app to Applications, then open it.
guide.macTwo: Follow the in-app instructions to allow Accessibility in System Settings → Privacy & Security. If keyboard monitoring is still unavailable, also allow Input Monitoring.
guide.macThree: Restart the app and press <kbd>Option</kbd> + <kbd>H</kbd> to show hints.
guide.macNote: The current macOS community build is not yet notarized by Apple. If macOS blocks it, follow the download verification and launch guide. You may need to grant permissions again after replacing the app.
guide.windowsTitle: How do I install on Windows?
guide.windowsBody: Run the installer and follow its steps, or extract the portable ZIP and run screen-buoy.exe. A system tray icon appears when it starts. Press Alt + H to show hints.
guide.windowsNote: Your configuration is created on first launch and kept when you upgrade.
guide.clickTitle: How do I right-click, double-click and exit?
guide.clickBody: Type a hint to click its target. Hold its last character to enter Hold mode, then press right <kbd>Shift</kbd> to right-click or <kbd>Enter</kbd> to double-click. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to exit hints at any time.
guide.clickNote: You can also hold <kbd>Space</kbd> to enter Hold mode at the current cursor position. Shortcuts are customizable.
guide.updateTitle: How do I update? Will my settings be kept?
guide.updateBody: Check for updates in the System tab of the app settings, then download and install the new version. Update signatures are verified and your personal settings are kept.
guide.updateNote: For older versions without an updater, download from this page and upgrade manually once. Downloads are also available on GitHub Releases.
guide.accountTitle: Do I need an account or browser extension?
guide.accountBody: No. Screen Buoy runs locally and uses native accessibility APIs to identify interface elements in browsers and other desktop apps. Detection depends on the accessibility elements each app exposes. Use grid hints for any remaining positions.
footer.tagline: Keep your thoughts moving. Keep your hands in flow.
guide.languageBody: The website detects your browser language. Use the selector at the top to choose another. App versions with localization follow your system by default; select a language or Follow system in the top-right corner of Settings. Your choice is saved automatically.
